questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: The QuickBooks Online test drive lets users explore a sample company called Craig's Design and Landscaping Services without creating an account or signing in. The guide specifies a direct URL to access this environment. Which URL opens the QBO test drive file?

explanations.a: The Student Guide specifies qbo.intuit.com/redir/testdrive as the direct link to access the QBO test drive file without creating an account.
explanations.b: qbo.intuit.com/login is the standard sign-in page for existing QBO accounts, not the test drive entry point.
explanations.c: quickbooks.intuit.com/online/compare is the subscription comparison page, not the test drive URL.
explanations.d: quickbooks.intuit.com/testdrive/start is not a URL listed in the Student Guide for accessing the test drive.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: After exploring the QBO test drive file and making various changes, a student closes the browser window. The test drive is designed so that any changes made are handled in a specific way when the session ends. What happens to data changes made in the QBO test drive when you log out?

answers.text: Changes are saved to a personal profile linked to the student's email
All changes are completely erased and the file is fully refreshed
Changes are stored temporarily for 24 hours before being erased
Changes are saved but hidden until the next session begins

explanations.a: The test drive is not linked to any user email or personal profile; it resets completely upon logout.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that when you log out of the test drive, all changes are erased and the file is completely refreshed.
explanations.c: The guide describes no 24-hour retention period; changes are erased immediately when the session ends.
explanations.d: Changes are not saved or hidden for future sessions; the test drive file resets entirely upon logout.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: Because QuickBooks Online is a web-based application, the browser a user chooses can affect performance and compatibility. The Student Guide identifies one browser as the preferred choice for the best QBO experience. Which browser does the Student Guide recommend for using QuickBooks Online?

explanations.a: Mozilla Firefox can be used as an alternate browser but is not the primary recommendation in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: Microsoft Edge is not identified as the recommended browser for QuickBooks Online in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: The Student Guide specifically recommends Google Chrome for the best QuickBooks Online experience.
explanations.d: Apple Safari is not identified as the recommended browser for QBO in the Student Guide.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: QuickBooks Online is offered at several distinct subscription tiers, each providing different features and user access limits. A student preparing for the QBCU exam needs to correctly identify how many subscription options QBO currently offers. How many subscription levels does QuickBooks Online offer?

explanations.a: Two tiers is incorrect; QuickBooks Online offers four distinct subscription levels.
explanations.b: Three tiers is incorrect; there are four subscription levels available in QuickBooks Online.
explanations.c: Five tiers is incorrect; QBO offers exactly four subscription levels.
explanations.d: QuickBooks Online offers four subscription levels: Simple Start, Essentials, Plus, and Advanced.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A bookkeeper working for a small business wants to use QuickBooks Online to enter vendor bills and pay them directly from within the software. The business currently subscribes to Simple Start and needs to upgrade. What is the minimum QBO subscription level that includes the ability to manage and pay bills from suppliers?

explanations.a: The ability to manage and pay bills from suppliers is introduced at the Essentials subscription level, making it the minimum required tier.
explanations.b: Plus includes bill management, but Essentials is the minimum tier that provides this feature.
explanations.c: Advanced includes bill management, but upgrading only to Essentials is sufficient for this need.
explanations.d: Business Pro is not a QuickBooks Online subscription tier; the four tiers are Simple Start, Essentials, Plus, and Advanced.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A law firm uses QuickBooks Online Plus and wants to confirm how many of its staff members can log in with full company access before exceeding the subscription's user limit. The office manager is planning user account assignments for the upcoming quarter. How many company users can access a QBO Plus subscription?

explanations.a: 3 company users is the limit for QBO Essentials, not Plus.
explanations.b: QBO Plus supports up to 5 company users who can access the QuickBooks Online file.
explanations.c: 10 company users is not a valid limit for any QBO subscription tier listed in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: 25 company users is the limit for QBO Advanced, not Plus.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A business owner comparing QuickBooks Online to QuickBooks Desktop wants to identify which QBO capabilities come included with every subscription tier at no extra charge beyond the monthly fee. The Student Guide highlights this as a key cloud-platform advantage. Which of the following features is included with all QBO subscription levels at no additional cost?

answers.text: Mobile app access for smartphones and tablets

explanations.a: Payroll processing requires an additional monthly fee on top of any QBO subscription and is not included for free.
explanations.b: Inventory tracking is available only in Plus and Advanced, not at all subscription levels.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that mobile access is included with all QBO subscription levels at no additional cost.
explanations.d: Scheduled bill payments through Bill.com are an add-on feature available in Essentials and above, not included free with every plan.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.objective: 1.4 Setting up a new QBO file
questions.text: A business has operated with QuickBooks Desktop for five years and is ready to transition to QuickBooks Online, intending to import the existing Desktop company file as the starting point. The Student Guide provides a specific recommendation for this migration scenario. What does the Student Guide recommend for businesses wanting to import an existing QuickBooks Desktop file into QBO?

answers.text: Use the QBO Setup Wizard and manually map the existing chart of accounts
Export all transactions to a CSV file and then import them into QBO manually
Call Intuit customer support to handle the migration remotely
Work with a QuickBooks ProAdvisor certified in QuickBooks Online

explanations.a: Manually using the Setup Wizard for a Desktop import is not the guide's recommendation; professional help is advised.
explanations.b: Exporting to CSV and manually importing is not the recommended migration approach described in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: Contacting general Intuit support is not the specific recommendation; the guide directs users to a certified ProAdvisor.
explanations.d: The Student Guide explicitly recommends contacting a QuickBooks ProAdvisor certified in QBO to handle Desktop-to-Online file migrations.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A sporting goods retailer wants to use QuickBooks Online to monitor stock levels, view quantity on hand on sales forms, and run a Physical Inventory Worksheet report. Inventory tracking must also be enabled in Account and Settings before it can be used. What is the minimum QBO subscription level that supports inventory quantity tracking?

answers.text: The plan that also includes purchase orders and supports up to five company users
The entry-level single-user plan that covers basic income and expense tracking
The mid-tier plan that first adds bill management and supports up to three users
The top-tier plan that includes Smart Reporting by Fathom and up to 25 users

explanations.a: Inventory tracking is available starting with QBO Plus, the plan that also includes purchase orders and supports up to five company users.
explanations.b: Simple Start — the entry-level single-user plan — does not support inventory tracking.
explanations.c: Essentials adds bill management and three users but does not include inventory tracking; that requires Plus.
explanations.d: QBO Advanced does support inventory, but it is not the minimum required tier; Plus is sufficient.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.objective: 1.2 Classes and locations limit in Plus
questions.text: A restaurant group on QBO Plus uses class tracking to separate financials by dining concept and location tracking to separate by physical site. As the business grows, they need to add more tracking segments but must stay within their subscription's combined cap. What is the maximum combined number of classes and locations allowed in a QBO Plus subscription?

explanations.a: 20 combined segments is not the correct cap for QBO Plus; the subscription feature matrix sets the limit at 40.
explanations.b: QBO Plus allows a maximum of 40 combined classes and locations, as shown in the Student Guide's subscription feature matrix.
explanations.c: 60 combined segments is not a limit listed for any QBO subscription tier in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Unlimited classes and locations is a feature of QBO Advanced only, not QBO Plus.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: An accounting firm manages QBO company files for clients across various subscription tiers, including Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus. A partner asks the firm's administrator how many accountant users or firms can be invited to each of these three subscription levels. How many accountant users or firms can be invited to a QBO Simple Start, Essentials, or Plus company?

explanations.a: One accountant user is not the correct limit; Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus each allow two accountant users or firms.
explanations.b: Three accountant users is the limit for QBO Advanced, not for the three lower tiers.
explanations.c: QBO Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus each permit up to two accountant users or firms to be invited.
explanations.d: Five accountant users is not a limit specified for any QBO subscription tier in the Student Guide.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A controller managing a QBO Essentials file is reviewing how many custom general ledger accounts the organization can create before hitting the system limit. The same ceiling applies equally to Simple Start and Plus subscribers. What is the maximum number of user-created general ledger accounts allowed in QBO Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus?

explanations.a: 100 accounts is not the correct maximum; QBO Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus each allow up to 250 user-created accounts.
explanations.b: 500 accounts is not the correct limit; the cap for these three tiers is 250 user-created general ledger accounts.
explanations.c: 150 accounts is not the correct limit for any QBO subscription tier described in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: QBO Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus each allow a maximum of 250 user-created general ledger accounts.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A merchandise company currently uses QuickBooks Desktop and values inventory using the weighted average cost method. They are evaluating a switch to QuickBooks Online and want to understand how their inventory valuation approach will change. How does QBO's inventory valuation method differ from that used by most QuickBooks Desktop editions?

answers.text: QBO uses first-in, first-out (FIFO); most Desktop editions use weighted average cost
QBO uses weighted average cost; most Desktop editions use FIFO
QBO uses last-in, first-out (LIFO); most Desktop editions use FIFO
Both QBO and most Desktop editions use weighted average cost, making the switch seamless

explanations.a: The Student Guide confirms that QBO uses the FIFO method for inventory valuation, while most Desktop editions use the weighted average cost method.
explanations.b: This reverses the correct relationship; QBO is the platform that uses FIFO, not Desktop.
explanations.c: QBO uses FIFO, not LIFO; LIFO is not a supported inventory valuation method in QuickBooks Online.
explanations.d: The two platforms do not share the same valuation method; QBO uses FIFO and most Desktop editions use weighted average cost.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: A wholesale distribution company wants to issue formal purchase orders to vendors before receiving merchandise, tracking open orders within QuickBooks Online. This feature must be activated under Account and Settings > Expenses before it becomes available as a transaction type. What is the minimum QBO subscription level that supports purchase order transactions?

answers.text: Purchase orders are not available in any current QBO subscription
The third subscription tier, which also includes inventory tracking and five-user access
The second subscription tier, which first adds bill management and three-user access
The fourth subscription tier, which includes unlimited classes and Smart Reporting by Fathom

explanations.a: Purchase orders are available in QBO Plus and Advanced; they are not absent from all subscription tiers.
explanations.b: QBO Plus — the third tier — is the minimum subscription that supports purchase orders; it also includes inventory tracking and up to five company users.
explanations.c: Essentials — the second tier — adds bill management and three users, but does not include purchase order functionality.
explanations.d: Purchase orders become available at the third tier (Plus), not exclusively in the fourth (Advanced).

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: During a sales presentation, an Intuit representative contrasts the reporting capabilities of each QBO subscription tier, starting from the entry-level plan and moving up to the top tier. The prospect wants to confirm the approximate number of built-in reports at each level. Which sequence correctly shows the approximate number of built-in reports moving from Simple Start through Essentials, Plus, and Advanced?

explanations.a: This sequence understates the reports at each tier; Simple Start alone includes over 20 built-in reports.
explanations.b: This sequence uses incorrect figures; Simple Start has 20+, not 15+, and Essentials has 40+, not 35+.
explanations.c: The Student Guide lists Simple Start at 20+, Essentials at 40+, Plus at 65+, and Advanced at 80+ built-in business reports.
explanations.d: This sequence overstates the counts at every tier and does not match the figures in the Student Guide's subscription matrix.

questions.name: QBO Setup & Subscriptions
questions.text: An enterprise client asks their accountant to recommend a QBO subscription that supports up to 25 company users, provides unlimited classes and locations for multi-unit tracking, and includes Smart Reporting by Fathom for KPI benchmarking across business units. The accountant reviews all four tiers before responding. Which QBO subscription satisfies all three of these requirements simultaneously?

answers.text: QBO Plus with the Smart Reporting add-on
QBO Essentials with advanced permission settings enabled

explanations.a: QBO Plus supports only 5 users and 40 combined classes and locations, and no Smart Reporting add-on exists for Plus.
explanations.b: QBO Essentials supports only 3 users, has no class or location tracking, and does not offer the described advanced permission settings.
explanations.c: QBO Plus supports up to 5 users and 40 combined classes and locations, which falls short of this client's requirements.
explanations.d: QBO Advanced supports up to 25 company users, unlimited classes and locations, and includes a license for Smart Reporting by Fathom.
